content: The guidelines published in August 2020 by the World Health Organization (WHO) focus on preventing HIV through safe, voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC) for adolescent boys and men in regions with generalized HIV epidemics. These guidelines provide detailed recommendations and key considerations for implementing VMMC as a public health intervention. The publication is available in both electronic and print formats, with respective ISBNs 978-92-4-000854-0 and 978-92-4-000855-7. The document includes acknowledgments of contributions from numerous individuals and organizations involved in its development. Members of the Guideline Development Group, external reviewers, and WHO staff provided technical expertise and feedback. The work was coordinated by the WHO Department of Global HIV, Hepatitis, and STI Programmes, with principal writers Julia Samuelson, Wole Ameyan, and Rachel Baggaley leading the effort. Funding for the development of these guidelines was provided by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and the United States President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR). The WHO Secretariat determined that there were no conflicts of interest requiring exclusion from the guideline development process. The guidelines define key terms such as adolescence, effective service coverage, medical male circumcision (MMC), and voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC). Adolescence is described as a critical phase of human development, encompassing individuals aged 10–19 years, with younger adolescents being 10–14 years old and older adolescents 15–19 years old. Effective service coverage is defined as the timely provision of health services at a quality level sufficient to achieve desired health outcomes. MMC refers to the complete surgical removal of the male penile foreskin performed by medical professionals, while VMMC specifically denotes MMC conducted with informed consent and without undue influence. The guidelines also highlight the importance of people-centered health care, which prioritizes the perspectives and needs of individuals, families, and communities. This approach ensures that health systems are organized around comprehensive needs rather than individual diseases and supports patients in making informed decisions about their care. Since 2007, WHO and UNAIDS have recommended VMMC as a key strategy for preventing heterosexually acquired HIV in men in regions with high HIV prevalence, particularly in East and Southern Africa. Over 23 million males have been circumcised through VMMC programs in these regions, with a significant proportion being adolescents aged 10–14 years. The guidelines underscore the importance of sustaining and expanding VMMC services as part of a comprehensive HIV prevention strategy, especially in light of other effective interventions such as antiretroviral therapy (ART) and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP).
